description: ConstellationEpheremides provides Python code for generating time-varying satellite ephemerides. Calum Turner documents its use to produce a simulated 1,584-satellite constellation modelled on phase one of Starlink. Users supply the constellation design, number of time steps and temporal resolution. The output is a ZIP archive containing CSV tables of positions, velocities and orbital elements for each spacecraft and step. Spatial coverage is low Earth orbit; the reference system and numerical accuracy are not stated in the short README. There is no fixed observation period because the data are generated from user settings. The repository contains the generator and documentation, is licensed under MIT and is free to obtain. It requires AstroPy and Poliastro. A separate IEEE DataPort dataset is linked but was not verified in this review; this record describes the available generator. Simulation uses include creating constellation inputs for connectivity and coverage studies. It relates to model-orbitpy-satellite-orbit-coverage, although direct interoperability and orbital propagation results were not tested.
name: ConstellationEpheremides megaconstellation ephemeris generator
